messages:
alice: FYI compliance pinged me — collection of KMS-related audit lines missing both actor and tenant_id. roughly 300 events in the last 24h.
ben: ugh, is this the same null-actor thing from last quarter? or new pattern?
alice: different footprint. last quarter was during the role-sync run. these look like requests routed through the new kms-proxy v2 we rolled Friday.
carol: @alice can you paste an example? I'll grep the sink.
auditbot: ALERT: 2026-03-19T23:12:11Z - audit_sink ERROR - event_id=ea3f2b actor=null tenant_id=null action="kms.encrypt" resource="projects/prod/key/foo"
dave: that log lines up with our canary deploy at 22:58. proxy v2 switched to forwarded-auth header handling.
ben: maybe the header mapping changed. we used to pull `x-caller-id` and `x-tenant` from the gateway. v2 might only pass the service token.
carol: ran a quick query: ```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events WHERE action LIKE '%kms.%' AND (actor IS NULL OR tenant_id IS NULL) AND ts > now() - interval '1 day';
-- result: 317
```
alice: 317 matches what compliance reported. they want proof of fix and a backfill plan.
dave: mitigation idea: if actor is null, map `service_principal` field (present) -> owner from mapping table. then annotate `actor_inferred=true` so audits are explicit.
ben: agree but we need to be careful — inferred actors are not as strong for compliance. should add a changelog and explain limitations.
carol: root cause likely the proxy dropped `x-forwarded-user` when it fell back to service auth. looking at code now — serializer does `headers.get('x-forwarded-user') || null`. v2 introduced `authorization: Bearer <svc-token>` handshake and lost upstream metadata.
alice: is this an engineering bug or intended behavior? compliance will escalate if it's a gap in auditability.
carol: engineering bug. we intentionally didn't strip headers but a middleware reorder in v2 ended up before header-injector.
dave: quick patch: reorder middleware so header-injector runs after auth middleware. will push a revert-like patch to canary.
ben: can we also add an audit log test to CI that asserts actor and tenant present for proxy-handled requests?
carol: yes, adding test now. also writing a backfill script that will attempt to reconstruct actor/tenant for the 317 events using request_id -> ingress logs and token mapping.
alice: timeline? compliance wants a short note by EOD.
dave: canary patch -> 15m. full rollout -> 2h if green. backfill script will run and produce artifacts in S3: `s3://redwood-audit/backfills/2478901234-recon/`
ben: small security question — when you reconstruct from ingress logs, we might surface sensitive headers. ensure backfill job runs in secure VPC and uses KMS to decrypt any secrets.
carol: yep, backfill runs in private subnet, KMS envelope decrypts the token map. no secrets dumped to logs.
alice: thanks. can someone @compliance with the mitigation plan? I'll draft the note.
dave: pinging @compliance: mitigation is in flight: patch rolling canary now, test added, backfill script queued.
auditbot: TICKET CREATED: #C-8492 - KMS audit missing actor/tenant - assigned to eng-security, priority=P1.
alice: assigning owners: @carol for patch & backfill, @dave for rollout, @ben for CI/test + compliance note review. I'll follow up with compliance writeup. :thumbsup:
carol: started PR: `fix/proxy-header-order` -> https://git.internal.redwood/repo/commits/abc123 
ben: thanks, will review CI changes.
alice: leaving this thread open, will update when compliance confirms.
carol: UPDATE 2478901478: canary looks good, no further null-actor events in the sink for the last 10m. backfill job started and has 0/317 unresolved so far.
alice: great work everyone. we'll keep the ticket open until backfill + compliance ack. :white_check_mark:
